Bank Indonesia Institute · Konsinyering JDSE · Session 3

Sustainable economy and finance research: trends, journals, and a place for JDSE

Research trends, the main journals, and Indonesia’s position. Based on 650,000 papers and four journal filters.

Arief Anshory Yusuf ·
Universitas Padjadjaran

Bandung, 15 October 2026

Background

Context, aims and method

Why this session, what it measures, and how

Context

Context: a new Bank Indonesia journal

The initiative

Bank Indonesia Institute (BINS) is designing a new journal: the Journal of Digital and Sustainable Economy and Finance (JDSE). This workshop drafts its concept.

What the TOR asks for

Aims and scope; positioning; frequency; priority themes; target authors and readers; editorial policy (double-blind review, open access, COPE ethics, APC); editorial structure; author guidelines; a roadmap from ISSN to SINTA, DOAJ and Garuda, with Scopus, WoS-SSCI and ABDC in the long run.

This session’s brief

Session 3: research trends, strategic issues and publication opportunities in sustainable economy and finance, as a basis for the journal. Session 2 covers the digital side.

Why bibliometrics

A new journal must choose its topics and its authors. Published papers show which topics grow, which are cited, which journals publish them, and where the authors are.

Source & method
Terms of reference, Konsinyering Penyusunan Rancangan Konsep JDSE, Bandung, 15 October 2026; BINS invitation letter.

Objectives

Four questions, each tied to an output the TOR asks for

ObjectiveWhat is measuredTOR output it informs
1. Which topics are growing?Growth by topic and journal filter. Themes that rose and fell. Digital × sustainable papers. Most cited papers.Fokus tematik, bidang kajian prioritas
2. Which journals publish this research?Main journals: index status, fees, citations. Time for new journals to enter Scopus. Central-bank journals. Open access.Positioning; kebijakan APC; target indeksasi
3. How much does Indonesia publish, and where?Indonesia’s share, rank, journals, institutions and topics, under four journal filtersTarget segmen penulis dan pembaca
4. Which themes should JDSE cover?Six standard tests: growth and citations, Q1 share, keyword map, sudden rises, Indonesia’s activity index, countriesAims and scope; call for papers; special issues

TOR section IV, Keluaran yang diharapkan.

Why topics, not keyword search

OpenAlex assigns every work up to three topics from 4,516, using title, abstract, journal and citations. Keyword search mis-assigns at scale: in the earlier SDG study, a quarter of papers tagged “innovation” were education research. Topic assignment avoids that.

Corpus rules

Sustainable corpus: primary topic in the six sustainable topics, 2010-2026, articles and reviews: 248,756 works. Digital corpus: any topic in the five digital topics: 398,142. Intersection: a work with one topic from each set. Keywords: OpenAlex’s own keyword field on each work.

Keyword search, used once

Scopus cross-check only: TITLE-ABS-KEY("sustainable finance" OR "green finance" OR "green bond*" OR "climate finance" OR "ESG investing" OR "ESG performance" OR "ESG disclosure" OR "ESG rating*" OR "sustainable banking" OR "transition risk" OR "carbon pricing" OR "green credit") AND PUBYEAR = <year> AND DOCTYPE(ar OR re). Run per year, alone and with AFFILCOUNTRY(Indonesia) and the ASEAN-6.

Source & method
Topic counts from the OpenAlex topics endpoint, all years and document types. Corpus counts are articles and reviews 2010-2026. A first version of the Scopus query used the bare word ESG, which also matched medical abbreviations before 2015; the ESG phrases are spelled out instead.

Part I · Research trends

Figure 2 · Green finance now dominates. Climate finance fell. Risk, ratings and greenwashing are new but still small

Biggest change: green finance

Green finance is in 36% of recent papers in all journals, up from 23%. In Q1 it rose from 10% to 31%. Papers on China rose from 3% to 14% in Q1.

Climate finance fell

Climate finance fell from 10% to 6% in all journals, and from 12% to 5% in Q1. Climate mitigation also fell.

New topics, still small

Transition risk, greenwashing and ESG ratings were near zero in 2015–2018. Now each is 3–5% of papers. Climate risk rose from 4% to 7% in all journals, but only from 8% to 9% in Q1. The early Q1 sample is small: 217 papers.

Source & method
OpenAlex keywords on works whose primary topic is Sustainable finance and green bonds, share of works carrying the keyword, 2015-2018 against 2023-2026, by journal tier. Keyword assignment is thinner for older works.

The topic is small and grows fast under all filters. No journal specialises in it. JDSE can be the first.

Part IV

Which themes should JDSE cover?

Six standard tests: growth and citations, Q1 share, keyword map, sudden rises, Indonesia’s strengths, and countries

Part IV · Themes for JDSE

Figure 15 · Growth and citations: ESG and green-finance themes at firm and market level grow fast and are well cited

Fast and cited, under both filters

ESG performance (100% a year, score 3.1), ESG ratings and disclosure, green finance, green bonds, corporate governance; in Q1 also green innovation, financial constraints and state-owned enterprises. Firm- and market-level questions with a measurable outcome.

Cited but slow

Climate mitigation and adaptation, carbon pricing, the Paris Agreement, energy transition: large and cited in all journals, but growing slower than the field. In Q1 they are at or below the Q1 average.

Fast but little cited

Sustainability reporting, the bare labels “sustainable finance” and “ESG”, green economy (score 0.4), environmental accounting (0.4), green transition. Many papers, few citations. A journal that accepts these papers easily will get many weak submissions.

Source & method
Each bubble a keyword; size = papers 2023-2025. Growth = compound annual growth of papers 2020 to 2025. Citation score = mean of citations divided by the same-year average of the filter, papers 2018-2023. Dashed lines: field growth (17% a year in all journals, 16% in Q1) and score 1. Red = above both.

Part IV · Themes for JDSE

Figure 16 · Share of each theme’s papers in Q1 journals

Climate, energy-transition and carbon-pricing papers reach Q1 more often than average. CSR, disclosure and green-economy papers reach Q1 less often. To attract Q1-level authors, JDSE must compete in the first group. In the second group it must be selective.

Source & method
26 largest themes by papers in all journals, 2016-2026. Red = above the field’s Q1 share.

Source & method
Kleinberg (2003) two-state burst model on each keyword’s yearly share of the filter, 2010-2025, s = 2, γ = 1. Bursts starting 2018 or later; → = still running in 2025. Strength = log-likelihood gain of the burst state, scaled to the strongest burst in each filter.

Part IV · Themes for JDSE

Figure 19 · Indonesia: strong in disclosure topics, weak in climate topics, cited below the world average

Where Indonesia specialises

Disclosure and governance variables: independent commissioners, audit committees, carbon-emission disclosure, environmental accounting. Activity index 6 to 9. The world cites these themes at 0.3 to 0.6 of average. Half of Indonesia’s keyword mentions are here.

Where it is absent

Climate adaptation, mitigation and policy, carbon pricing, emissions trading, the Paris Agreement, energy transition, green bonds: activity index 0.2 to 0.5. The world cites these themes above average.

Within each theme

Indonesia is also active in some well-cited themes: corporate governance, ESG disclosure, greenwashing. But its own papers are cited below the world in 95% of themes. The median gap is 0.6 of average. So the issue is quality within themes, not only the choice of themes.

Source & method
Activity index = (Indonesian papers in the theme / all Indonesian papers) / (world papers in the theme / all papers), 2016-2026, all journals. World citation score as in Figure 15. Under the Scopus filters Indonesia has too few papers per theme for a stable index.

Part V

What this means for JDSE

Limits of the evidence, then six recommendations

Part V · What this means for JDSE

Limits of the data and the method

OpenAlex on authors

Good for counting papers. Less good for author affiliations: some institution records merge similar names. Institution counts are approximate.

Topics and keywords

Topic assignment is a classifier, not a human judgement. Keyword coverage is thinner before 2020, so early shares are lower bounds and growth is overstated for new keywords.

Scopus matching by ISSN

A journal counts as Scopus only if an ISSN matches the September 2026 list. Title changes and missing ISSNs undercount Scopus by a few per cent.

Citations

Total citations to date, not by year. Recent papers have had less time; the citation score compares papers of the same year to correct for this. 2024-26 papers are excluded from it.

Time

2026 is a partial year and is never plotted as a full one. Growth is 2015-2025 or 2020-2025.

Not done

Reference age (novelty), citation velocity by year, newcomer authors, funding and policy citations. Each needs a second download.

Source & method
OpenAlex reliability: own institution check in the research-quality study (three of 25 largest Indonesian institution records conflated, excluded there).

Implications

What the evidence implies for JDSE

1 · Focus on digital × sustainable finance

4,640 papers in all journals, 1,977 in Q1. The fastest growth under every filter (Figures 1 and 3). No specialist journal yet. Put it in the title, the aims and the first call.

2 · Cover the themes that grow fast and are cited

ESG performance and ratings, green finance and green bonds, climate and transition risk, greenwashing (Figures 2, 15 and 18). Avoid themes one country dominates, such as state-owned enterprises (Figure 20). First special issue: ESG ratings and climate risk, the youngest cluster (Figure 17).

3 · Serve emerging-market authors

Indonesia is 2nd in the world in all journals and 32nd in Q1 (Figures 11 to 14). The authors exist. They lack a journal. Start with ASEAN-6, then India, Pakistan and Vietnam (Figure 8). Use calls and reviews to move Indonesian authors from disclosure topics to climate and finance topics (Figure 19).

4 · Free to publish, and indexed

No fee for readers or authors. 28% of all papers are diamond, but only 2% of Q1 papers (Figures 9 and 10). Apply to DOAJ in year one. Apply to Scopus after two years of regular issues (Figure 7).

5 · Require data and code; publish policy briefs

Every empirical paper shares its data and code. Each paper has a two-page policy brief. Few journals in the field do this. BI has analysts who can support it.

6 · Track the journal’s metrics from the start

Citations, author countries, topics and index status, from OpenAlex, on a public page. Baseline: BMEB, h-index 33, two citations per paper in two years.

Source & method
Each card points to the figure that supports it.
